# gitmoap_team_access (Data Source)

The access a team holds, on the groups and repositories you can see. A grant on a group or repository you cannot see is left out of the page and only counted.

The token needs `team:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "acme" {
  full_path = "acme"
}

resource "gitmoap_team" "reviewers" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
  name     = "Reviewers"
  slug     = "reviewers"
}

data "gitmoap_team_access" "example" {
  team_id = gitmoap_team.reviewers.team_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `team_id` (String) Team ID

### Read-Only

- `grants` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--grants))
- `hidden_scopes` (Boolean) Whether the team also holds access somewhere you cannot see. Those places are never named.

<a id="nestedatt--grants"></a>
### Nested Schema for `grants`

Read-Only:

- `at` (Attributes) A group or repository, as the access API names one. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--grants--at))
- `created_at` (String)
- `expires_at` (String)
- `grant_id` (String)
- `granted_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--grants--granted_by))
- `reason` (String)
- `role` (Attributes) A role — built in or defined by the organization — with its display name and the built-in rank
it counts as. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--grants--role))

<a id="nestedatt--grants--at"></a>
### Nested Schema for `grants.at`

Read-Only:

- `full_path` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `type` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--grants--granted_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `grants.granted_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.


<a id="nestedatt--grants--role"></a>
### Nested Schema for `grants.role`

Read-Only:

- `builtin` (String)
- `custom` (String)
- `name` (String) The role's display name: a built-in name such as `Developer`, or the custom role's name.
- `rank` (String)
